This matches the claim exactly.

*   **Camera Motion Cancellation:** If the camera moves at the same speed as the primitives, motion should cancel out, but because the motion blur is baked into the voxel buffer via accumulated velocity, this cancellation is not possible, leading to incorrect blur [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that if the camera moves at the same speed as the primitives, motion should cancel out, but because motion blur is baked into the voxel buffer via accumulated velocity, this cancellation is not possible, leading to incorrect blur. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'We find another problem if the camera is moving at the same speed as the primitives being rasterized, any motion should be cancelled out and the result look sharp. But because the motion blur is baked into the voxel buffer this is not possible.' This directly supports every part of the claim.
